en: For the Country, for the Ancestors
Let us march united, let us march united
In our ranks no traitors
Of the soil let us be sole masters
Let us march united, let us march united
For the Country, for the Ancestors
Let us march, march, march united
For the Country, for the Ancestors
For the Forefathers, for the Fatherland
Let us dig joyfully, let us dig joyfully
When the field bears fruit
The soul grows strong
Let us dig joyfully, let us dig joyfully
For the Forefathers, for the Fatherland
Let us dig, dig, dig joyfully
For the Forefathers, for the Fatherland
For the Country and for our Fathers
Let us raise Sons, let us raise Sons
Free, strong and prosperous
We shall always be brothers
Let us raise Sons, let us raise Sons
For the Country and for our Fathers
Let us raise, raise, raise Sons
For the Country and for our Fathers
For the Forefathers, for the Fatherland
O God of the Valiant, O God of the Valiant
Under your infinite protection
Take our rights, our life
O God of the Valiant, O God of the Valiant
For the Forefathers, for the Fatherland
O God, O God, O God of the Valiant
For the Forefathers, for the Fatherland
For the Flag, for the Fatherland
To die is beautiful, to die is beautiful
Our past cries out to us:
Have hardened souls
To die is beautiful, to die is beautiful
For the Flag, for the Fatherland
To die, to die, to die is beautiful
For the Flag, for the Fatherland
notes: 'Ancêtres' is rendered Ancestors and 'Aïeux' Forefathers, as the original uses two words.
line 3.2: 'Formons des Fils', literally 'let us form sons': raise and train them.
line 4.2: 'Preux', the valiant, the brave (an old word for knights).
